A1.goal: Recognise a situation, changes in voice and a few basic instructions.

gist.title: Why does the speaker gather the men?
options: To tell them how to behave
To teach them a song
To choose a new leader
gist.why: He sets rules for the celebration.

gist.title: Does his voice stay quiet from beginning to end?
options: Yes, he whispers
No, he begins to shout
Yes, he sings
gist.why: His voice gets louder as he repeats the warning.

detail.title: Which celebration is he trying to protect?
options: A birthday
A sports match
A wedding
detail.why: The speaker is concerned about a wedding.

detail.title: What does he want to stop at the event?
options: People fighting
People eating
People dancing
detail.why: The repeated main instruction is not to fight.

detail.title: Why does he mention Grace?
options: She is the band's singer
He does not want her to feel embarrassed
She is driving the guests home
detail.why: Protecting Grace from embarrassment is a reason for his rules.

sequence: He explains why this day matters.
Other men interrupt him with questions.
He repeats his warning more loudly.

facts.title: Write the first name of the woman the speaker wants to protect.

open.title: Describe the speaker's voice in one short sentence.
open.answer: He becomes angry or shouts while giving rules.
open.criteria: Accept stressed, angry or increasingly loud if grounded in the clip.

A2.goal: Understand the purpose of the exchange and selected concrete details.

gist.title: What is the main problem the speaker wants to prevent?
options: A delay in the ceremony
A fight between groups
A problem with the music
gist.why: He fears trouble among the wedding guests.

gist.title: How do the interruptions change his speech?
options: They make the conversation less controlled
They help him finish calmly
They cause him to forget why he came
gist.why: Interjections distract him and interrupt his orders.

detail.title: What clothing leads to a complaint?
options: School uniforms
Coats for cold weather
Official uniforms
detail.why: A listener objects that some people are in uniform.

detail.title: Why does the speaker keep talking about his bride?
options: He wants guests to avoid embarrassing her
He needs help choosing her dress
He is asking her to speak to the men
detail.why: He frames restraint as a matter of respect for Grace.

detail.title: What does he do when one man brings up an odd topic?
options: He changes to a friendly conversation
He gives a series of firm refusals
He invites everyone to join in
detail.why: The unexpected interruption triggers emphatic refusals.

sequence: He announces that the day is important.
A member of the group mentions a broken promise.
He begins listing behaviour that will not be allowed.

facts.title: What kind of clothing was the speaker told would not be present?

open.title: Give one reason the speaker seems nervous about the wedding.
open.answer: There may be bad feeling between guests, and he fears a public scene.
open.criteria: Accept reference to group tension, possible fighting or Grace's embarrassment.

B1.goal: Follow the key conflict, specific restrictions and changes in tone.

gist.title: What makes the scene more than a simple list of wedding rules?
options: A conflict over who is in control
A sudden change to a different location
A long discussion about music
A quiet talk between two friends
gist.why: The orders and challenges reveal a struggle over authority.

gist.title: How does the contrast between the subject and the speaker's tone affect the scene?
options: It makes every instruction easy to accept
It gives a serious warning an unexpectedly comic edge
It suggests the wedding has already finished
It proves that nobody is listening
gist.why: A demand for peace delivered with anger can also be funny.

detail.title: What had the speaker apparently promised about the people at the event?
options: Everyone would bring their own food
The gathering would be very small
There would be no uniforms
All guests would follow a written plan
detail.why: The objection refers to an earlier promise about uniforms.

detail.title: Why is his reference to Grace persuasive within the group?
options: He makes the consequences personal rather than merely practical
He promises that Grace will reward every guest
He says the bride has already left
He wants the group to choose a new host
detail.why: He asks them not to embarrass the bride.

detail.title: Why does he turn towards a particular man later in the conversation?
options: To ask him to organise the music
To challenge him about stories he has been telling
To give him responsibility for the ceremony
To request help from a family member
detail.why: One listener is singled out for telling stories about the speaker.

sequence: He explains the importance of the occasion.
One of the men disputes an earlier promise.
A seemingly unrelated question interrupts the warnings.
The speaker addresses one person directly.

facts.title: What name does the speaker use for the group in uniform?

open.title: Explain one moment when the other men make it difficult for the speaker to stay in control.
open.answer: A complaint about uniforms or the question about snow breaks his argument, forcing him to respond.
open.criteria: Accept a named interruption with its effect on his speech.

B2.goal: Understand what is meant but not said, idioms, and how the characters relate to each other.

gist.title: Which contradiction creates much of the scene's effect?
options: The men are asked to keep order by somebody who speaks aggressively
The bride is absent but still gives orders
The speaker wants a quiet wedding with no guests
The gathering is described as a business meeting
gist.why: The speaker demands restraint while raising his voice and threatening consequences.

gist.title: What does the exchange reveal about the speaker's relationship with the men?
options: He has no authority over them at all
He is listened to but frequently challenged or interrupted
He prefers to discuss each rule patiently
They never question his promises
gist.why: Interruptions test his attempt to control the conversation.

detail.title: Why does the objection about the uniformed guests matter?
options: It is only a complaint about fashion
It proves the ceremony has ended
It recalls an unresolved source of tension between groups
It shows the men were invited by accident
detail.why: Uniforms symbolise a group that may provoke the speaker's men.

detail.title: What does the speaker communicate by invoking Grace's feelings?
options: The rules are meant to protect someone else from embarrassment
She expects him to read a speech aloud
The guests have already embarrassed her
She has asked for a different wedding venue
detail.why: Grace becomes a personal reason to avoid conflict.

detail.title: What does the speaker seem to mean when he accuses a man of telling stories?
options: The man has published a fictional book
The man has been describing him in a possibly misleading way
The man knows the programme for the event
The man is repeating the official guest list
detail.why: The expression concerns stories or claims about the speaker, not literal fiction.

sequence: He reminds the men of the significance of the day.
A listener objects to the presence of uniforms.
An awkward question interrupts his attempt to warn them.
He becomes more direct and personal in his orders.

facts.title: Name the man the speaker confronts about telling stories.

open.title: Explain how the interruption about 'snow' changes the tone of the scene.
open.answer: It shifts a threatening address into an unexpected, almost comic exchange before the speaker resumes restrictions.
open.criteria: Accept a balanced answer recognising comic interruption and continuing tension.

C1.goal: Interpret indirect meanings, interpersonal power, idiomatic speech and comic incongruity.

gist.title: What is the main paradox of the speaker's attempt to establish discipline?
options: He performs authority through language that itself becomes increasingly uncontrolled
He asks the men to leave without giving any reason
He is prevented from speaking throughout the clip
He insists that nobody may disagree at a wedding
gist.why: A demand for peaceful conduct is delivered in heated, coercive language.

gist.title: What do the interruptions reveal about his command of the exchange?
options: His position is automatically accepted
Authority must be asserted repeatedly in an unstable group conversation
His emotional appeals have no effect
He abandons all attempts to control the men
gist.why: Other speakers challenge or redirect him, requiring repeated attempts to reclaim the floor.

detail.title: How does the short reply after the protest about uniforms operate?
options: It accepts the complaint and changes the guest list
It asks the protester to explain his point
It acknowledges a challenge while allowing the speaker to proceed
It implies the speaker had forgotten his promise
detail.why: The concessive response overrides the objection rather than resolving it.

detail.title: What rhetorical purpose does concern for the bride serve?
options: It gives a moral and emotional reason for obedience
It makes the instructions less serious
It invites the bride to settle the disagreement
It removes the possibility of conflict
detail.why: He frames obedience as avoiding harm to Grace's dignity.

detail.title: Why might the accumulation of prohibitions be comic as well as threatening?
options: Every prohibited action is impossible at a wedding
The speaker combines extreme seriousness with oddly specific forms of misbehaviour
The listeners are already following every rule
The list is delivered as a calm formal announcement
detail.why: The detailed bans juxtapose menace with incongruous possibilities.

sequence: He invokes the importance of the occasion.
An earlier agreement is challenged.
An incongruous question breaks the flow.
He returns to increasingly specific prohibitions.

facts.title: Which word does the speaker use for the group he considers a possible provocation?

open.title: Analyse one way the dialogue undermines the speaker's attempt to perform authority.
open.answer: A protest or off-topic remark disrupts his monologue, exposing the need to negotiate or reassert control.
open.criteria: Require a specific conversational event and an explanation of its pragmatic effect.

C2.goal: Critically analyse power, register and comic timing in authentic colloquial dialogue.

gist.title: Which account of power is most strongly supported by the excerpt?
options: Power is asserted through speech but continually renegotiated by interlocutors
The speaker's commands are accepted without response
The wedding removes previous social tensions
The men abandon the event before any rules are stated
gist.why: Repeated interventions make dominance an ongoing interactional achievement.

gist.title: How is the scene's humour best understood?
options: It erases the possibility of violence
It grows out of the collision between high-stakes threats and mundane interruption
It depends entirely on the characters misunderstanding a word
It transforms the wedding into an official debate
gist.why: Comic bathos arises within, not outside, the threatening setting.

detail.title: What does the speaker's concessive response to an objection demonstrate?
options: A willingness to concede the entire disputed point
An inability to hear other speakers
An attempt to register resistance without yielding conversational control
A plan to abandon the rules
detail.why: The response both recognises the protest and reasserts the speaker's agenda.

detail.title: How does concern for the bride change the interpersonal stakes?
options: It shifts the rationale for obedience towards protecting a third party
It proves the bride has already complained
It makes the conflict purely a private disagreement
It shows that the men have no knowledge of the ceremony
detail.why: He gives public restraint an emotional justification tied to Grace.

detail.title: What is a plausible explanation for the escalating volume of the final rule?
options: He wants the recording to be heard at a distance
It increases coercive intensity while potentially revealing fragile control
He is telling the men a different story
It signals he has forgotten the audience
detail.why: Shouting both asserts authority and may betray anxiety about compliance.

sequence: He frames the occasion as requiring unusual restraint.
An earlier agreement is disputed.
A tangential question produces an abrupt tonal shift.
The speaker attempts to restore authority through a string of bans.

facts.title: What first name does the speaker use for the bride?

open.title: Evaluate whether the profanity in the scene functions mainly as solidarity, intimidation or loss of control.
open.answer: The familiar register signals in-group belonging but the same words exert coercive pressure and may reveal anxiety.
open.criteria: Accept a nuanced interpretation with evidence from turns, interruptions or repeated orders.
